title: MUSCLE MANGA - Kaoru Hanayama's Physique in Grappler Baki (part. 1)
summary: NH profiles Kaoru Hanayama from Grappler Baki: the narrative hype around him, his grip-based fighting, his fights with Tommy, Yuri and Baki, his tattoo and family backstory, and his genetically gifted, monstrous physique. He uses the character to note that genetics have their place even in a story built on hard work.
claims: Exposition about an unseen antagonist is the best way to hype a manga character; Kaido in One Piece is the best example
Hanayama is introduced as a 15-year-old yakuza boss who beat 50 armed men in under 30 minutes and can tear coins
Tearing a coin by hand appears to be impossible in real life, even for men with very strong grip
Hanayama is drawn at 6'3 and 365 lb at 15, without the skinniness usually seen in tall teens
Flipping a ~5000 lb Cadillac would make him almost 5 times stronger than the real tire flip world record of about 1350 lb
His physique: neck and traps three times the size of his head, tree-trunk legs, massive core and chest, ripped rather than fat; not even 50 years of training would give that body
Hanayama has the anabolic jawline, a trademark of the most badass Baki characters like Yujiro and Jack
Hanayama's strength was purely genetic; by age 10 he crushed glass bottles in his hand
Even though Baki insists on hard work, genetics still matter, as in real life; there is no point whining about it, but some people are born with superior physical abilities
Grip strength is a powerful weapon; Hanayama relies on it to crush limbs and even grab the floor
In a martial arts story size is not everything; much of Baki is about beating larger, more muscular opponents
